rules.why: A filter then a map walks the array twice. Use one flatMap or a lazy iterator pipeline.
`as unknown as T` throws away the type evidence. Parse the value instead.
`...(c ? { x } : {})` hides an optional field. Build the object with its real type.
A wide annotation on a known value throws away what the checker knows.
A parameter of type `object` accepts anything. Name the type the function needs.
A reduce that copies its accumulator on each step is quadratic.
Reflect.apply hides the call from the type checker. Call the function.
Reflect.get hides the read from the type checker. Read the property.
A function that returns `unknown` makes each caller parse its result.
An alias of `unknown` gives a name to a type with no evidence.
`Record<string, unknown>` is a bag with no checked keys. Model the keys.
A value widened to `unknown` and asserted back is an unchecked cast.
A reduce that spreads its accumulator is quadratic. anti-slop pairs it with no-reduce-accumulator-copy.
A promise that nobody awaits drops its error. The rule is type-aware, so it also proves that tsrs runs.
Caught errors have one name. `cause` is also allowed, because anti-slop/no-unknown-parameters accepts no other name on a catch callback.
A module mock tests the wiring, not the behavior. Inject the dependency.
A typeof check on a typed value repeats what the types say. Keep typeof inside type guards.
A `Shape` name describes the structure, not the domain concept.
An `unknown` parameter leaves input unparsed. Parse at the boundary and accept the domain type.
Blank lines between statement groups keep code readable. `oxlint --fix` adds them.
Each `as` cast states the invariant that makes it safe, in a `SAFETY:` comment.
Each disable comment gives its reason after `--`.
Keeps the preset's `@nocommit` ban and bans the `oxlint-disable` spelling, which require-description does not read.
